exposure: Niemann-Pick disease type C1 (NPC1) status (diseased, carrier, control)
outcome: Levels of 3b,5a,6b-trihydroxycholanic acid (bile acid A) in dried blood spots
Levels of trihydroxycholanic acid glycine conjugate (bile acid B) in dried blood spots
Feasibility of newborn screening for NPC1
cohort: The study included newborn dried blood spots (DBS) from 15 already diagnosed Niemann-Pick disease type C1 (NPC1) subjects, 3 NPC1 carriers, and two neighbor controls for each, all residing in California, New York, and Michigan.
finding: Newborn screening for Niemann-Pick disease type C1 is feasible using bile acid biomarkers, with bile acid A consistently elevated in all NPC1 subjects, demonstrating better long-term stability in archived DBS compared to bile acid B.
cross-section timing: Newborn period (using archived dried blood spots collected at birth)
